What the AI Boom Looks Like From Inside Cisco with Sam Badri | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 77

Cisco IR chief Sam Badri explains accelerating networking demand, a campus refresh cycle and expected fiscal-2027 growth. Eisman accepts the reality of AI-related sales while concentrating on lab dependence and price competition. Badri presents advanced workflows as a source of future token growth and a reason frontier models can retain a premium. Verified financial disclosures support current growth and NVIDIA receivables concentration, but they do not settle final-user returns, long-run supplier profitability or the competitive outcome.

Steve Eisman interviews Cisco investor-relations chief Sam Badri. Guest operational assertions and forecasts are kept separate from Eisman's questions and explicit final synthesis.

  • Badri represents Cisco and discusses company guidance; these are not independent realized forecasts.
  • His investor-conversation sample does not establish the claimed 90% beginner share.
  • NVIDIA 70% refers to receivables, not revenue.
  • The concluding summary adopts conditional durability, not every guest numerical or technical assertion.

How he reasons here

  • Separate genuine supplier revenue from durable final-user economics.
  • Distinguish customer mix effects from vendor competitive performance.
  • Map premium and inexpensive models to the tasks that require them.
  • Track token volume alongside price, cost, retention and cash collection.
